audit.why: Poppy-favoured early with Skill at 6 matches the 56.17% win rate over 324 games and the packet chart; Kassadin's pre-6 melee weakness against a 475-range wall-stun is real.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike says Riftwalk is 'on a long early cooldown and costs him HP'. Riftwalk's cooldown is 5/3.5/2 seconds and its cost is 40 mana, escalating with repeat casts — no health cost at all.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Multiple Riftwalks in a short period of time cost additional Mana.' The kit lists cd 5/3.5/2, cost 40.
audit.corrected: Spike, whys[4] and the mid text now key the bait to his mana pool rather than an imaginary long cooldown or HP cost.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three places call Null Sphere a silence. Riot's text has no silence — it deals damage, interrupts channels, and shields Kassadin against magic damage. The late text even says it 'silences your engage'.
audit.why: The real interaction is the reverse of what the page implies: Null Sphere reaches 650 and interrupts channels, so it cancels Keeper's Verdict, which is cast at 500 range and flagged as a channel. That is the decisive late-game interaction and it was missing.
audit.corrected: Silence removed everywhere; Null Sphere's 650-range channel interrupt against Poppy's 500-range R channel stated in the late text. Also added the Nether Blade auto-reset wind-up as the burst tell, and W stopping the Riftwalk blink to slow and ground him.

edits.before: You both have weak Level 1s, but your single Q already chunks his max HP while his Q silence barely scratches your tankiness — deny his last-hits.
edits.after: You both have weak Level 1s, but your single Q already chunks his max HP while Null Sphere only buys him a small shield — deny his last-hits.

edits.before: His R blink is up but on a long early cooldown and costs HP; bait it, then E-wall him before it refreshes for the kill.
edits.after: Riftwalk is only a 5s cooldown but each repeat costs more mana; force the blinks, then E-wall him once he is dry for the kill.

edits.before: His R blink is up but on a long early cooldown and costs him HP — bait it, then E-wall him before it refreshes.
edits.after: Riftwalk costs 40 mana and escalates per cast — force repeat blinks, then E-wall him the moment he runs dry.

edits.before: This is your window to make the lane unwinnable for him. At 6 his R blink is up but on a long early cooldown and chips his own HP, so bait it out, then E-wall him before it refreshes. Keep W ready to ground him when he tries to blink in or out — denying his repositioning is the whole point. Your Q max-HP damage is gold-independent, so even off a CS deficit you out-trade him every all-in through Levels 4-6.
edits.after: This is your window to make the lane unwinnable for him. At 6 Riftwalk is a 5s cooldown but 40 mana that escalates per cast, so force repeat blinks and E-wall him once he is dry. Keep W up to stop the blink itself — a caught Riftwalk leaves him slowed and grounded, and denying his repositioning is the whole point. Your Q max-HP damage is gold-independent, so you out-trade him every all-in through Levels 4-6.

edits.before: Once Rod of Ages and a Rabadon's come online, Kassadin flips the matchup — he blinks in and out of your W range every few seconds, silences your engage, and bursts you with magic damage before you can wall-stun. You do not out-scale him; your kit value flatlines. The plan is to make the early lead matter: deny his CS, take his tower, and force the map to close before ~20-25 minutes. If it goes long, group with your team and use W and R to peel rather than chasing his blink solo.
edits.after: Once Rod of Ages and a Rabadon's come online, Kassadin flips the matchup — he blinks every 2 seconds at rank 3, and Null Sphere's 650 range interrupts your 500-range Keeper's Verdict channel before it lands. If it goes long, group with your team and use W and R to peel rather than chasing his blink solo.

edits.after: Trade against his mana, not his cooldown: Riftwalk escalates in cost. Nether Blade's auto wind-up is the burst tell, not the cast.
